title: Sleep "comes" in Korean 😴 잠이 와요 #learnkorean
caption:
잠이 와요 (jami wayo) = I'm sleepy — literally "sleep comes."

Korean uses one verb, 와요 (wayo, "comes"), for all of these:
잠이 와요 — I'm sleepy
친구가 와요 — my friend is coming
비가 와요 — it's raining
눈이 와요 — it's snowing
전화가 와요 — I'm getting a call

가 or 이? Same job: 가 after a vowel (친구가, 비가), 이 after a consonant (잠이, 눈이).

pinnedComment: What else "comes" in Korean? Guess it in the comments 👇 (hint: 봄 = spring)
alt: A cozy needle-felted café. A coral felt ghost mascot sits by a cup of coffee while a small fluffy sleep cloud drifts in through the window; it lands on its head and the mascot gets sleepy (잠이 와요 · jami wayo · Sleep comes. = I'm sleepy). A friend in a mustard sweater opens the café door and waves (친구가 와요), rain pours outside the window (비가 와요), snow falls (눈이 와요), a phone buzzes and the mascot jumps (전화가 와요). At the end everything arrives at once: the friend waves, snow falls, the phone buzzes — and the mascot, fighting to stay awake under a card listing the five sentences with 와요 lined up, finally falls asleep. Last line: Sleep comes. 잠이 와요.
